summary: Franz Woepcke was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin (1843–1847), studied at the University of Bonn (~1844–1850), and studied under Georg Freytag, Julius Mohl, and Philippe Édouard Foucaux. He taught mathematics at Französisches Gymnasium Berlin (1856–1858).

Tibetologist Franz Xaver Erhard earned degrees from Humboldt University of Berlin (M.A., 1996–2001), Free University of Berlin, University of Bonn, and University of Leipzig (Dr. phil., 2010–2015). He held posts at Oxford (2016–2017, 2019) and served as Visiting Professor for Tibetology at Leipzig (2022–2023).

Franz Xaver Miklosich worked in linguistics and Indology, earning a Ph.D. at Graz (~1830–1838) and a law doctorate at Vienna (~1838–1841). He served at the Austrian National Library (1844–1862) and became extraordinary professor of Slavic philology and literature at Vienna in 1849.

Franz von Erdmann, an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist, studied at Rostock (~1812–1815) and Göttingen (~1815–1818). After serving as privatdozent at Rostock in 1818, he was Professor of Oriental languages at Kazan State University (~1818–1845).
Franz von László was an Indologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1941 and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Bonn (~1948–1952) under doctoral supervisor Willibald Kirfel.

Franz-Karl Ehrhard worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning degrees and habilitation at the University of Hamburg (~1974–1998) under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as Resident Representative for the Nepal Research Centre (1988–1993) and as Professor at the University of Munich (2001–2019).
François Grimal is an Indologist who held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and served as Director at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~2002–2008).

François Gros was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon (~1950–1954) and under Pierre Meile and Jean Filliozat. He served as Directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1977–2002).
François Lachaud is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who held a professorship at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2008 and 2013).

François Martini, an Indologist and linguist, studied at INALCO (~1920–1922) and under Sylvain Lévi. He was a professor at INALCO (1928), General Secretary of the Buddhist Institute, and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1957–1965).
François Voegeli is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who held posts at Kyoto University (attested 1998) and the University of Lausanne (attested 2012–2014 as Senior FNS Researcher).
François-Marie Bertrand was an Indologist who studied at the Séminaire de Saint-Sulpice and was taught by Garcin de Tassy.

Françoise L'Hernault worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied at INALCO, Annamalai University, and Sorbonne Nouvelle (Ph.D. by 1984), and managed photographic collections at the École française d'Extrême-Orient starting in 1971.

Françoise Mallison is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Charlotte Vaudeville. She succeeded Vaudeville in 1988 and served as Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Tibetologist and historian-archaeologist Françoise Pommaret studied at the Sorbonne (~1974–1979), INALCO, and the University of Paris. She served as Director of Langues et cultures de l'aire tibétaine (~2004–2008) and Directeur de recherche at CNRS (starting 2002).

Françoise Robin is a Tibetologist who earned a DEA at INALCO and a doctorate under Heather Stoddard. She served as Director at the Collège de France (2009–2015) and led the Tibetan Department (2011) and Southeast Asia/Pacific Department (2013–2014) at INALCO.

Fred Henry Andrews worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was vice-principal at the National College of Arts (1890), curator at Lahore Museum (~1890–1899), art department director at Battersea Polytechnic (~1899–1910), and principal at Sri Pratap Technical College (1914).

Fred Pfeil worked in Buddhist studies and other fields, earning degrees from Amherst College (~1967–1971) and Stanford University (~1971–1973). He taught at Stanford, Stephens College, Oregon State University, and Trinity College, Hartford (~1983–2005).

Fred Walter Householder, Jr. was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vermont (A.B. through 1932) and Columbia University (A.M. ~1932–1934; student of Louis H. Gray). He taught at Columbia, Allegheny College, and Indiana University Bloomington (1948–1983).

Freda Bedi worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at St Hugh's College (~1929–1933) and with Mahasi Sayadaw (~1952–1953), and she founded the Young Lamas Home School and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling Nunnery.
